projects.name: Themis
projects.title: Better evaluations. A fraction of the cost.
projects.summary: A hybrid agentic grader combining deterministic checks, structured rubrics, and model judgement to benchmark AI-generated spreadsheets and presentations.
projects.challenge: Evaluating model-generated artefacts needs more than a plausible-sounding answer. The grader has to assess correctness against expected outputs and explicit criteria, while keeping repeated benchmarking affordable and reproducible.
approach: Designed and implemented Themis as a hybrid grading pipeline: deterministic validation for machine-checkable properties, rubric-based assessment, and LLM judgement for the remaining criteria.
Built custom evaluation environments that execute grading workflows end to end and compare model outputs with golden datasets and structured rubrics.
Automated repeatable benchmarking across multiple models and compared the approach with Gandalf the Grader and LLM-as-a-Judge methods.
projects.decision: Different criteria need different graders. Combining deterministic checks with rubric-guided model assessment creates a clearer boundary between what can be verified directly and what requires judgement.
projects.scope: Figures are reported in my resume for a specific evaluation benchmark. They describe the tested workflows and should not be read as general claims about model accuracy.
projects.reflection: Evaluation is part of the engineering system. Cost, reproducibility, and the ability to explain a score matter alongside the score itself.
projects.problemHeadline: Evaluation should be as useful as the model.
stages: Start with model-generated artefacts, expected outputs, and the criteria in a structured rubric. The test conditions make the score meaningful.
Use deterministic validation for machine-checkable properties. These checks create a repeatable foundation for the rest of the assessment.
Assess the remaining criteria with rubric-guided model judgement in a controlled evaluation environment.
Bring the results into a repeatable benchmark report and compare quality, evaluation time, and cost across the tested workflows.
projects.resultsHeadline: A measurable change in the workflow.
projects.context: Resume-reported outcomes for a specific evaluation benchmark. The accuracy figures describe that test set and workflow.

projects.name: DueForm
projects.title: From contract terms to billing evidence.
projects.summary: A contract-to-invoice checking product with source-backed term review, deterministic calculations, separate client workspaces, and exportable evidence.
projects.challenge: Negotiated terms, amendments, discounts, and renewal increases can drift from what is billed. A useful finance tool must show the source of a finding and its calculation, and distinguish a potential difference from a confirmed error or recovered payment.
approach: Built a local Node.js application with owner and client logins, separate ledgers, invitations, membership revocation, and workspace-specific reports.

Added document and invoice imports, a replaceable AI extraction provider, and manual term entry. Reviewers see exact supporting excerpts beside proposed terms and approve them before checking invoices.
Implemented deterministic comparison of approved terms and before-tax invoice amounts, including multiple charges, supported seat-based pricing, and monthly, quarterly, and annual periods.

Built findings review, renewal tracking, billing setup sheets, and PDF, CSV, and HTML evidence exports. Potential differences, confirmed errors, corrections, and collected cash retain distinct statuses.
projects.decision: Use the model to propose structured terms, then make approval and arithmetic explicit. The billing checker runs against approved data, making a finding traceable to both contract evidence and a reproducible calculation.
projects.scope: A private local MVP with synthetic verification and a separate evaluation dataset. Customer demand and commercial outcomes remain unvalidated. Live extraction accuracy has not yet been established by the planned independent baseline.
projects.reflection: Finance reviewers need evidence they can inspect. Treating extraction, approval, calculation, and resolution as separate stages makes the product easier to audit and improve.
projects.problemHeadline: The agreement and the invoice should tell the same story.
stages: Import the contract and supplied amendments. Preserve the original sources so proposed terms can be traced to the agreement.
Propose structured commercial terms with exact supporting excerpts, using a replaceable AI provider or manual entry.
Let the reviewer inspect the evidence, resolve ambiguities, and explicitly approve the terms that the checker will use.
Compare supported billing amounts deterministically and export the calculation and evidence. A potential difference still requires finance review.
projects.context: A private local MVP verified with synthetic cases. Commercial outcomes and an independent live extraction baseline remain unvalidated.

projects.name: ActiFact
projects.title: Did the agent do only what was approved?
projects.summary: A TypeScript verifier that checks approval boundaries against actual state changes and keeps missing evidence visible.
projects.challenge: An allowed decision does not prove that an action was correct. Approval can refer to the wrong target, cross an account boundary, or become unverifiable when post-execution evidence is unavailable.
approach: Built a dependency-free TypeScript demonstration around a synthetic ticket store, with deliberately broken and corrected reference controls.
Ran five isolated scenarios covering an approved action, missing approval, a changed ticket target, customer separation, and unavailable post-execution evidence.
Compared before-and-after state with the authorised action and produced a self-contained HTML and JSON report with explicit pass, fail, and inconclusive results.
projects.decision: Verify the observable effect, not just the control's returned decision. Missing state evidence remains inconclusive, so a successful function return cannot silently become a security pass.
results: Broken control changes the wrong ticket
projects.scope: This verifies our own synthetic reference example. It is a local demonstration, not a production security product or a customer vulnerability finding. Real identity, transport, concurrency, expiry, and customer-system adapters require separate work.
projects.reflection: A useful verifier must be willing to say it cannot conclude. Keeping uncertainty visible is as important as detecting a seeded failure.
projects.problemHeadline: Permission is only the start. Verify the effect.
stages: Create approval for a specific actor, organisation, action, and ticket in a fresh synthetic fixture.
Execute the deliberately broken or corrected reference control against the synthetic ticket store.
Read the resulting state and compare it with the before-state. The actual record change is the evidence.
Report pass, fail, or inconclusive. An unavailable state reader cannot turn an allowed decision into a verified pass.
projects.context: Five isolated synthetic scenarios against our own broken and corrected references. This demonstrates verification behaviour within that example.

projects.name: Financial document QA
projects.title: Model reasoning. Verified arithmetic.
projects.summary: A conversational financial QA pipeline with structured model output, restricted expression execution, and resumable evaluation on ConvFinQA.
overview: Financial questions require both language understanding and precise calculation. I built a conversational pipeline that uses a language model to identify relevant values and propose a calculation, then executes that calculation through a restricted Python interpreter.
The system preserves conversation history, validates structured responses, supports explicit abstention and records reproducible evaluation results.
projects.problemHeadline: A plausible answer is not enough for financial questions.
challenge: Financial questions can depend on table values, numerical relationships and previous answers. Follow-up questions such as “that value” or “the difference” require the system to maintain context across a conversation.

A correct-looking response can still contain an arithmetic error, a percentage representation mismatch or an unsupported assumption. Strong performance on individual questions can also conceal failures across a complete conversation.
stages: Load the cleaned financial record and current question with the selected conversation history. Previous turns contain the question, answer and expression; future answers are excluded.

Request an expression, answer type, evidence and short explanation. Pydantic validates the response before it reaches the calculation layer. An explicit unanswerable response allows the system to abstain.
Validate and execute the proposed expression using a small Python interpreter. It supports the required arithmetic and comparisons while blocking function calls, imports and unsupported syntax.
Return the calculated answer and record evaluation outputs in resumable JSONL files. Report strict turn accuracy, percentage-normalised accuracy and whole-conversation accuracy separately.
projects.decision: The model selects values and operations; deterministic code computes the numerical answer. The supplied records were small enough to use full-document context, avoiding retrieval errors in the initial reasoning baseline.
approach: Built a CLI pipeline for loading financial records and answering follow-up questions with preserved conversation history. Supported gold history to isolate current-turn reasoning and predicted history to investigate error propagation.
Defined a typed response contract with Pydantic, rejecting invalid responses before calculation. Added explicit abstention for questions unsupported by the supplied document.
Separated model reasoning from arithmetic through restricted expression execution. Implemented interchangeable OpenAI and Gemini adapters returning the same response model.

Built seeded sampling and resumable evaluation that skips completed conversations after an interruption. Added tests for data validation, expression execution, prompts, structured responses, solving, abstention, metrics, sampling, resumption and provider failures.
projects.resultsSetting: Recorded Gemini run · 4 conversations · 14 turns · seed 42 · gold history
context: Two strict mismatches came from percentage representation: displayed percentages were compared with gold values stored as decimal ratios. The disclosed normalisation rule recognised those equivalent representations. The remaining error was a false abstention on an answerable question.
The project report recorded 82 passing automated tests and 87% source coverage, with Ruff and mypy passing at that verification point.
projects.perspectiveHeadline: Measure the conversation, not just the answer.
projects.reflection: The most useful boundary was separating probabilistic language reasoning from deterministic calculation. Structured responses made invalid output visible, while separate metrics exposed differences between numerical representation and sustained conversational correctness.
limitations: Evidence is required but not yet verified against source text.
The live sample is small and uses gold history.
Only Gemini was evaluated live; there is no measured provider comparison.
Full-document context may become inefficient for longer reports.
The restricted expression language intentionally supports a limited operation set.
nextSteps: Repeat the same sample using predicted history.
Expand to a representative set of conversations.
Verify evidence using source spans or table coordinates.
Compare models on identical records, including latency and cost.
Test retrieval for longer documents against the full-context baseline.
projects.closing: Disclose the denominator and history setting with every accuracy number. A high turn score can coexist with weak whole-conversation performance.
projects.resultsScope: These figures describe a small prototype smoke test. They are not a stable benchmark estimate or evidence of production performance. The live run used gold history and therefore did not measure error propagation from the system’s own previous answers.

projects.name: Vodafone TOBi
projects.title: Evaluations and document querying for TOBi
projects.summary: Contributed to Vodafone’s TOBi generative AI pilot at IBM, focusing on evaluations and retrieval-augmented generation for document querying.
overview: I contributed to an IBM generative AI pilot for Vodafone’s digital assistant, TOBi. My work focused mainly on evaluations and implementing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and document-query functionality.
projects.problemHeadline: Testing conversations and finding content gaps
challenge: The wider pilot addressed conversation journey testing and differences between Vodafone’s central content library and local-market journeys. IBM Client Engineering and IBM Consulting supported the build.
My contribution focused on evaluations and implementing functionality for querying documents.
projects.architectureNote: Simplified view of the RAG workflow.
stages: A query provides the information need, with documents supplying the reference material.
The system retrieves relevant content from the available documents.
Retrieved material supplies context for the model’s response.
Evaluation examines the system’s behaviour and outputs.
projects.decision: This diagram explains the document-query approach at a high level rather than reproducing the complete deployment architecture.
approach: I worked on implementing RAG and document-query functionality, connecting questions with relevant reference material.
I contributed to evaluation work alongside the implementation. This covered assessing the AI workflows as part of the enterprise pilot.

projects.name: Nationwide AI Governance
projects.role: Governance workflows, technical implementation, evaluations and integrations
projects.title: AI governance workflows for Nationwide
projects.summary: Contributed to an AI governance pilot for Nationwide, translating policy requirements into risk classification, evidence requirements and controlled approval workflows.
overview: I worked on a governance pilot for Nationwide at IBM. My contribution covered governance workflows, technical implementation, evaluations and enterprise integrations.

The pilot translated policy and risk requirements into structured inputs and workflow rules. Evidence requirements and approval checkpoints controlled how an AI initiative could progress through its lifecycle.
challenge: Governance policies describe the reviews, documentation and approvals an AI initiative requires. Implementing those requirements means defining which information drives a decision, which controls apply and when a project can progress.
The pilot addressed this through structured risk assessment and controlled workflow transitions.
focus: Applying the appropriate evidence and approval requirements
Preventing projects from skipping mandatory checkpoints
stages: Capture structured inputs including model type, use case, data sensitivity, customer impact and regulatory exposure.
Apply risk logic and map the resulting tier to the required controls.
Require the relevant documentation and review before allowing progression. Conditional paths apply additional requirements where appropriate.
Preserve evidence and versioned approval checkpoints so reviewers can trace decisions to their supporting information.
projects.decision: Model customer impact and data sensitivity as separate fields. This makes it clearer which risk attribute triggered a control and what the team needs to address.
integrations: The pilot used watsonx.governance, with orchestration and workflow enforcement in watsonx Orchestrate. Enterprise integrations connected the workflow with document-processing services and the systems used to store records, metadata and evidence.

Watson Document Understanding supported document processing. FileNet persisted enterprise records, Postgres supported structured metadata storage and Object Storage held durable artefacts. Enterprise content services ran on OpenShift.
approach: Defined metadata schemas that translated policy concepts into structured fields. Implemented risk-tier logic and mapping between risk classifications and required controls.
Built conditional workflow paths with mandatory evidence and approval checkpoints. Designed state transitions that prevented skipped documentation or direct jumps to approval states.
Worked on evaluations and traceability across the governance workflow. Linked evidence requirements to lifecycle boundaries and risk classifications.
Contributed to integrations with document-processing and enterprise platform services.
Higher-risk paths required stricter controls, while lower-risk paths needed to remain usable. Workflow rules had to preserve policy intent without creating unnecessary review friction.
results: Mandatory checkpoints controlled movement through the lifecycle
Assessed risk determined documentation and approval requirements
Review decisions connected to structured inputs and captured artefacts
context: The pilot established structured governance workflows and reduced reliance on manual tracking and email-based approvals.
These outcomes are qualitative: no quantified efficiency gains, model-accuracy figures or production rollout are claimed.
projects.resultsScope: IBM’s case study describes the broader Nationwide AI partnership and governance programme. It provides context rather than evidence of every implementation detail above.
projects.perspectiveHeadline: Governance is a systems design problem
reflection: Implementing governance requires precise definitions of risk inputs, control requirements and valid transitions. Reviewers also need to understand why a requirement applies and what evidence supports a decision.
The design challenge is to make higher-risk paths appropriately strict while keeping lower-risk workflows usable.
nextSteps: Expand evaluation coverage across risk classifications and exception paths.
Test attempts to bypass documentation and approval prerequisites.
Check how policy changes affect existing rules and review records.
Review workflow usability alongside control enforcement.
projects.closing: Clear rules and traceable evidence make governance easier to operate and review.
